content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High error and latency spike observed on serving pool rwd-eu-3. Metric: continuous_batcher.kv_cache_evictions/sec spiking x100. Paging on-call (mike-oncall). Priority: P1. Links: https://sentry.internal/r/12345, dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/serving/kv-cache.

mike-oncall: on it. saw the page, grabbing context. any immediate customer-facing impact?

elaine: +1 high 95/99 latencies on text-generation endpoints. A few customers reporting timeouts and increased cost. In the last 5m: 17% of prod requests saw >3s extra latency, and token cost jumped ~40% for some workloads.

raj: looks like KV cache blowups — keys not TTL-ing due to batch config change rolled last night (PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/serving/commit/4f2a3d). continuous_batcher now holds larger prefixes and batching windows.

mike-oncall: can we confirm cause quickly? set up heap/kv metrics?

ops-bot: Auto-checks: disk pressure OK. GPU utilization normal. KV-cache size (rwd-eu-3): 2.1x expected; eviction rate up; continuous_batch_window_ms set to 250 (was 100).

kevin: that config change was the feature-flag roll for larger batch windows to improve throughput for long-context workloads. Flag: ff/continuous_batch_increase. Deployed to 100% last night at 02:14 UTC.

mike-oncall: rollback plan? We should either flip the feature flag back to 100->0, or use per-customer override to reduce window for affected customers. Which is least risky?

elaine: Recommend immediate rollback to mitigate customer impact. Canary rollback to 5% first? If this is causing eviction storms, even 5% might help but slower to reduce overall pressure. I'd flip globally to 0, then canary the improved change later.

raj: Agreed. The KV cache eviction is nonlinear — small percentage of requests can amplify. Global rollback fastest. I have a mitigation play: set ff/continuous_batch_increase=off across all serving nodes and also set per-customer override for the few largest customers to ensure stable baselines.

mike-oncall: do it. raj, do the flag flip and post commands. elaine, start incident comms for customers. kevin, keep an eye on the deployment systems.

raj: Running command (k8s ff control plane):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"continuous_batch_increase","env":"prod","state":"off"}' \
  https://ff-control.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/toggle
```
Response: 200 OK — rollout initiated (targeting all serving clusters).

ops-bot: Feature-flag deployment propagated to 85% of nodes after 60s, 100% after 2m 10s.

support-bot: Customer-facing note drafted: "We're investigating increased latency and cost for text-generation. Engineers have rolled back a recent batcher config change to stabilize performance. We'll share an update in 30 minutes." Should I post to status.redwood?

mike-oncall: yes post now. include affected endpoints and a brief mitigation note.

elaine: Posted. Channel: #status, status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2024-03-batch-config. Included known affected customers (internal list).

kevin: monitoring graphs show p95 dropping back toward baseline. KV cache size trending down after flag flip. Eviction rate back to expected within ~180s window.

mike-oncall: good. we need a short postmortem timeline and next steps: root cause, hotfix strategy, and rollout plan for reintroducing change safely.

raj: quick root cause summary: change increased continuous_batch_window_ms from 100->250ms and expanded prefix retention heuristics. Unexpected workload pattern for prefix-heavy customers caused large numbers of unique KV keys to be cached, exhausting memory limits and triggering eviction storms that degraded performance and increased token re-computation costs.

elaine: Customer impact: 6 enterprise customers reported timeouts/retries; estimated 12 hours of degraded performance across the cluster window. Billing impact: temporary token cost surge; finance notified.

mike-oncall: Hotfix plan for reintroducing safely: 1) revert PR and keep flag off. 2) implement per-customer override capability in flag service to limit window to 100ms for sensitive customers. 3) add canary rollout with traffic-shaping to 1%/5%/25%/100% with 30m observation windows and automatic rollback on defined SLO breaches (p95 latency increase >20% or KV-evictions >2x baseline). 4) add additional telemetry: per-prefix key cardinality histograms and cache memory pressure alarms.

kevin: I can push a new variant flag that supports a numeric param instead of binary: continuous_batch_window_ms={value}. We'll default to 100 for prod, and canary to 150 for low-risk customers. PR drafted: https://git.internal/r/redwood/serving/pull/887.

raj: propose per-customer override flow: feature-flag API accepts "overrides": {"customer_id":1234, "window_ms":100}. ops will use this to protect top 10 noisy customers during rollout.

mike-oncall: we should also add a safe-guard in runtime: hard cap on per-node KV entries for any single prefix (e.g., 50k keys) and per-tenant eviction thresholds. If a single prefix tries to exceed limit, we drop caching for that prefix and emit an event.

elaine: Adding that guard ASAP would help long-term; file a follow-up ticket. For now, include it in the postmortem action items.

ops-bot: Post-rollback monitoring: 10m ago p95=210ms (baseline 190ms), token-cost spike subsiding. No further customer escalations in the last 12 minutes.

support-bot: Notified the 6 affected customers with a summary and apology, and offered a follow-up call. All customers acknowledged; two asked for technical details which eng will provide.

mike-oncall: Next actions: (1) kevin — finish param-flag PR and canary automation; (2) raj — implement per-customer overrides and add API docs for ops; (3) elaine — write customer-impact section for postmortem and coordinate a follow-up customer call; (4) me — draft incident timeline. Aim: roll safe reintroduce in 48 hours after additional telemetry and canary automation.

kevin: On it. PR will include automated rollback hooks tied to the new SLO checks. Also adding a flag preview endpoint so SRE can simulate flag values per-customer.

raj: will land per-customer override endpoint and a one-click UI in the ops console. Commands for emergency per-customer override (example):
```
POST /api/v1/flags/override
{
  "flag":"continuous_batch_window_ms",
  "env":"prod",
  "overrides": [{"customer":"acme-corp","value":100},{"customer":"beta-inc","value":100}]
}
```
Response: 200 — overrides applied in ~30s.

mike-oncall: Good. Please update runbook section "batcher-regressions" with steps we just exercised: flip flag, per-customer override, emergency cap, and how to contact SRE.

elaine: I'll start the incident doc in the ops drive and add notes on customer comms.

kevin: small test suggestion: before full re-rollout, run a synthetic workload that simulates high-prefix cardinality to validate the cap behavior. I can schedule that in staging now.

mike-oncall: OK. we'll call this mitigated for now. Keeping the channel open for follow-ups. If anything spikes again, page immediately and include the new flags playbook.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> partial: Flag reverted. Monitoring continues. Incident channel will remain open for 24h.

elaine: thanks all. Postmortem owners: raj (root cause + runtime guard), kevin (flag rework + canary infra), mike-oncall (timeline + runbook updates), elaine (customer comms).

kevin: estimate to have canary infra and telemetry in 36-48 hours. I'll post PRs in this thread when ready.

raj: adding postmortem task list: add per-prefix cardinality metric, implement per-tenant caps, add canary auto-rollback at 5m and 30m windows, and update the feature-flag service to support numeric params and overrides.

support-bot: closing customer notifications: all customers contacted, 2 follow-ups scheduled.

mike-oncall: thanks everyone. closing now but keeping watch. :thumbsup:
